title: War throughout the land
summary: In the seventy-second year of the reign of the judges, contentions increase and wars occur throughout the land among the people of Nephi. A secret band of robbers carries on destruction and wickedness. The war lasts through that year and the seventy-third year.

explicit_facts.text: In the seventy-second year of the reign of the judges, contentions increase and wars occur throughout all the land among the people of Nephi.
A secret band of robbers carries on destruction and wickedness.
The war lasts through the seventy-second year and continues in the seventy-third year.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A broad, non-specific view of conflict can convey the reported widespread wars.
unspecified_visual_details: The combatants' clothing, weapons, and the locations of particular conflicts are not specified.
The appearance of the secret band of robbers is not specified.

narration.text: there were wars throughout all the land among all the people of Nephi.
And it was this secret band of robbers who did carry on this work of destruction and wickedness.
And this war did last all that year; and in the seventy and third year it did also last.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report a war spanning two years; they do not describe a particular battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the secret band of robbers or give its members invented identities.
Do not depict a specific battle, leader, or act of destruction as a documented event.
Do not merge the seventy-second and seventy-third years into a single moment.

title: Nephi prays for famine
summary: Nephi cries unto the Lord and asks that famine, rather than the sword, stir the people to remembrance and repentance.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi cries unto the Lord.
Nephi asks that the people be spared destruction by the sword and that famine stir them to remembrance and repentance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is praying; the verse does not specify where.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's posture, surroundings, and appearance are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: O Lord, do not suffer that this people shall be destroyed by the sword;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: but O Lord, rather let there be a famine in the land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict famine beginning during this prayer; it follows in the account.

title: Famine grips the land
summary: The famine comes as Nephi asked. The sword's destruction ceases, but famine brings destruction; dry earth yields no grain, and thousands perish in the more wicked parts of the land among both Nephites and Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: A great famine falls upon the people of Nephi; destruction by the sword ceases but destruction by famine becomes severe.
The earth is dry and yields no grain; thousands perish in the more wicked parts of the land, among Lamanites as well as Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Dry, uncultivated fields can represent the stated failure of the earth to yield grain.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular settlements, crops, victims, and manner of death are not specified.

narration.text: there was a great famine upon the land
the earth was smitten that it was dry

prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore or identify specific people among those who perish.

title: The people remember
summary: As the people see they may perish by famine, they remember the Lord and Nephi's words. They plead with their chief judges and leaders to ask Nephi to pray for the famine to cease.

explicit_facts.text: The people see that they are about to perish by famine and begin to remember the Lord and Nephi's words.
The people plead with their chief judges and leaders to ask Nephi to cry unto the Lord to turn away the famine.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People pleading before leaders is a visual rendering of their stated request.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and identities of the people and leaders, and where they meet, are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, we know that thou art a man of God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people (reported request)

spoken_dialogue.text: and therefore cry unto the Lord our God
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people (reported request)

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Nephi present in the appeal; the people request that leaders send the message to him.

title: Nephi prays again
summary: The judges relay the requested words to Nephi. Seeing the people repent and humble themselves in sackcloth, Nephi prays, noting that the Gadianton band has become extinct and asking the Lord to turn away his anger.

explicit_facts.text: The judges speak to Nephi as the people had desired; Nephi sees the people repent and humble themselves in sackcloth, then prays.
Nephi says the people have swept away the band of Gadianton, which has become extinct, and concealed its secret plans in the earth.
Nephi asks the Lord to turn away his anger.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi can be shown praying while the repentant people in sackcloth are visible in the setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The place of prayer, the judges' location, and the specific means by which the band was swept away are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: O Lord, behold this people repenteth;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: and they have swept away the band of Gadianton from amongst them
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the destruction of the band or the concealment of plans as a new present-tense action.

title: A prayer for rain
summary: The speaker petitions the Lord to end the famine and send rain, recalls an earlier petition and promise, states that the people have repented, and asks the Lord to try again whether they will serve him.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker asks the Lord to turn away his anger and end the famine.
The speaker requests rain so the earth may produce fruit and grain in season.
The speaker recalls requesting famine so the pestilence of the sword would cease, and reports the Lord's earlier conditional promise to spare the people if they repent.
The speaker says the people have repented because of famine, pestilence, and destruction.
The speaker asks the Lord to try again whether the people will serve him and says the Lord can bless them according to his words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained depiction of the speaker addressing the prayer to the Lord can accompany the petitions.
unspecified_visual_details: The supplied verses do not state the speaker's name, appearance, clothing, posture, or surroundings.
Time of day and the presence of any listeners are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: O Lord, wilt thou turn away thine anger, yea, thy fierce anger, and cause that this famine may cease in this land.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Speaker of the prayer

spoken_dialogue.text: Yea, O Lord, and thou seest that they have repented, because of the famine and the pestilence and destruction which has come unto them.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Speaker of the prayer

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The role label does not assert that the speaker is a new or different person; identification from preceding verses is outside the supplied source.
The earlier petition and the Lord's earlier promise are recollections within the prayer, not new present events.
Rain and renewed agricultural production are requested, not narrated as occurring.
prohibited_inventions: Do not supply a personal name from material outside these verses.
Do not invent a visible appearance or present spoken response from the Lord.
Do not show rain arriving, crops recovering, or the famine ending.
Do not stage the recalled petition, warfare, destruction, or the people's repentance as simultaneous present action.
Do not invent listeners or additional dialogue.

title: Rain and harvest return
summary: In the seventy-sixth year the Lord turns away his anger and rain falls; the earth brings forth fruit and grain in their seasons.

explicit_facts.text: In the seventy-sixth year the Lord causes rain to fall, and the earth brings forth fruit and grain in season.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Rain falling on the earth and fruit and grain growing are visual depictions of the stated events.
unspecified_visual_details: The crops, landscape, and extent or duration of rainfall are not specified.

narration.text: caused that rain should fall upon the earth
it did bring forth her grain

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure; the verse does not describe an appearance.

title: Rejoicing and renewed respect
summary: The people rejoice and glorify God, no longer seek to destroy Nephi, and esteem him as a great prophet and man of God. Lehi, his brother, is likewise righteous.

explicit_facts.text: The people rejoice and glorify God; they no longer seek to destroy Nephi and esteem him as a great prophet and man of God.
Lehi, Nephi's brother, is not behind him in righteousness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People rejoicing and glorifying God can be depicted as a collective response.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of glorification and the physical appearance or precise location of Nephi and Lehi are unstated.

narration.text: the whole face of the land was filled with rejoicing
Lehi, his brother, was not a whit behind him

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words spoken by the people, Nephi, or Lehi.

title: Rebuilding and spreading
summary: The people of Nephi begin to prosper again, rebuild their waste places, multiply, and spread across the land from sea west to sea east.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Nephi prosper again, build up waste places, multiply, and spread across the land from the west sea to the east sea.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Rebuilding and settlement can be represented by people repairing structures and occupying land.
unspecified_visual_details: Building styles, specific settlements, and individual builders are not stated.

narration.text: began to build up their waste places
from the sea west to the sea east

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names to settlements or depict specific structures as historical facts.

title: Peace and a spreading church
summary: The seventy-sixth year ends in peace. The church spreads throughout the land and most Nephites and Lamanites belong to it; the people have great peace, with only a few doctrinal contentions in the seventy-eighth year.

explicit_facts.text: The seventy-sixth and seventy-seventh years are peaceful; the church spreads throughout the land, and most Nephites and Lamanites belong to it.
There is peace in the seventy-eighth year except for a few contentions concerning points of doctrine laid down by prophets.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A peaceful gathering of people may convey the stated peace and spread of the church.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific gathering, church building, or doctrinal dispute is described.

narration.text: they did have exceedingly great peace in the land
a few contentions concerning the points of doctrine

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific doctrinal argument or assign its participants.

title: Preaching ends strife
summary: In the seventy-ninth year, Nephi, Lehi, and many brethren who know true doctrine and have daily revelations preach to the people and put an end to strife that same year.

explicit_facts.text: Much strife begins in the seventy-ninth year.
Nephi, Lehi, and many brethren preach to the people and end the strife that same year.
The preachers know true doctrine and have many revelations daily.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi, Lehi, and their brethren can be shown preaching to a gathered audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The teaching venue, specific doctrines, and audience members are not identified.

narration.text: they did preach unto the people
they did put an end to their strife

prohibited_inventions: Do not create sermon dialogue or depict revelations as visible supernatural events.

title: A war begins
summary: In the eightieth year, Nephite dissenters who had joined the Lamanites and some Lamanite descendants begin war against their brethren. They murder and plunder, retreat into remote places, hide, and gain recruits.
characters: Nephite dissenters who joined the Lamanites

explicit_facts.text: In the eightieth year, dissenters from the Nephites who had joined the Lamanites and some Lamanite descendants begin war against their brethren.
They murder and plunder, retreat to mountains, wilderness, and secret places, hide, and receive additions to their numbers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The beginning of war may be represented by the attacking group confronting their brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The combatants' names, exact location, clothing, weapons, and the specific acts of murder or plunder are not detailed.

narration.text: they commenced a war with their brethren
they did commit murder and plunder

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named combatants or show graphic injury.

title: The robbers grow
summary: Over time the robbers become an exceedingly great band, search out Gadianton's secret plans, and become Gadianton robbers, bringing great destruction among Nephites and Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: The band grows exceedingly great, searches out the secret plans of Gadianton, and becomes Gadianton robbers.
The robbers cause great havoc and destruction among Nephites and Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A large group can visually suggest the reported growth of the band.
unspecified_visual_details: The secret plans' contents and how the robbers cause destruction are not specified.

narration.text: they became an exceedingly great band of robbers
great destruction among the people of Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Gadianton himself; the verses do not say he is present.

title: An army enters the wilderness
summary: An army of strong men is sent into the wilderness and mountains to search for and destroy the robbers. In that same year, the army is driven back into its own lands.

explicit_facts.text: An army of strong men is sent into the wilderness and mountains to search out and destroy the band of robbers.
In the same year, the army is driven back into its own lands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The army may be shown advancing through wilderness or mountain terrain in its search.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities of the army and robbers, the specific encounter, and how the army is driven back are not stated.

narration.text: they sent an army of strong men into the wilderness
they were driven back even into their own lands

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The expedition and its retreat occur as separate events; do not collapse them into a single moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a named commander or a particular battle.

title: The second expedition retreats
summary: Early in the eighty-first year, the army again goes against the robbers and destroys many, while also suffering much destruction. It returns from the wilderness and mountains because the robbers' numbers there are so great. The robbers continue to increase and defy the Nephite and Lamanite armies, causing widespread fear.

explicit_facts.text: Early in the eighty-first year, the army again attacks the robbers; many robbers are destroyed, and the army also suffers much destruction.
The army returns from wilderness and mountains because of the great number of robbers there.
The robbers continue to grow strong, defy the Nephite and Lamanite armies, and cause great fear throughout the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A retreating army and a larger opposing group can convey the reported imbalance in numbers.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific battle, army losses, robbers' appearance, and source of fear are not detailed.

narration.text: did destroy many; and they were also visited with much destruction
the exceeding greatness of the numbers of those robbers

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict graphic injuries or identify particular casualties.

title: Robbers carry people captive
summary: The robbers visit many parts of the land, kill many, and carry others captive into the wilderness, especially women and children. This evil stirs the people to remember the Lord; the eighty-first year ends.

explicit_facts.text: The robbers bring destruction to many parts of the land, kill many, and carry others captive into the wilderness, especially women and children.
The evil that comes because of the people's iniquity stirs them again to remember the Lord their God.
The eighty-first year ends.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A non-graphic depiction of captives being led toward the wilderness can represent the reported captivity.
unspecified_visual_details: The captives' identities, precise route, and the location of the attack are unstated.

narration.text: did carry away others captive into the wilderness
stir them up again in remembrance of the Lord their God

prohibited_inventions: Do not show graphic killing or imply any specific captive's fate beyond the text.

title: The people turn again to wickedness
summary: In the eighty-second year the people begin to forget the Lord; in the eighty-third they grow strong in iniquity; in the eighty-fourth they do not mend their ways. In the eighty-fifth they grow in pride and wickedness, ripening again for destruction, and the year ends.

explicit_facts.text: In the eighty-second year the people begin to forget the Lord; in the eighty-third they grow strong in iniquity; in the eighty-fourth they do not mend their ways.
In the eighty-fifth year they grow stronger in pride and wickedness and are ripening again for destruction.
The eighty-fifth year ends.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group engaged in ordinary activity can convey the reported return to pride and wickedness without inventing particular acts.
unspecified_visual_details: No individual behavior, setting, or specific manifestation of pride and wickedness is described.

narration.text: they began again to forget the Lord their God
they were ripening again for destruction

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Ripening” is figurative language in the account, not a literal visible transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not turn the figurative phrase into a supernatural visual event or invent specific wicked acts.
